grounding.states: Toyota Sienna is the pick: Edmunds ranks the 2026 Sienna #1 and Quartz calls it the clear choice for best overall minivan
grounding.from: Edmunds ranks the 2026 Toyota Sienna #1. / Quartz (about 18 days old) picks the Sienna. It calls the Sienna the clear choice for the best overall minivan.

grounding.states: Sienna is also named #1 by Yahoo/AutoGuide
grounding.from: A Yahoo/AutoGuide four-way comparison (about 55 days old) also puts the Sienna first. It names the Toyota Sienna the #1 winner.
MSRP is $41,320 to $58,710, with 35–36 mpg combined.
It has a standard hybrid powertrain and available all-wheel drive.
U.S. News notes the hybrid system is noisy.

grounding.states: Honda Odyssey drives most like a car
grounding.from: It drives the most like a car, with responsive steering and a smooth V6.

grounding.states: Honda Odyssey is front-wheel drive only

grounding.from: KBB lists it at $44,245 starting, 22 mpg combined.

grounding.states: Odyssey is ranked best by U.S. News and at the top of KBB's list
grounding.from: U.S. News ranks the Honda Odyssey best. / KBB currently has the 2026 Honda Odyssey at the top of its list.

value.answer: For the US, I'd go with the Toyota Sienna. It's the most efficient of the bunch at 35-36 mpg combined, you can get it with all-wheel drive, and Edmunds, Quartz and AutoGuide all have it on top. The hybrid system can be noisy, though. If you'd rather have something that drives like a car, the Honda Odyssey is the one U.S. News and KBB put first, but it's front-wheel drive only and gets 22 mpg.
